main_text.p: loquenti, quasi contentione Rhetorica caussam illustra-re, ac fusius docere, quibus potissimum in rebus vera pœnitentia sita sit, quidq; Dominus pro placatione desideret vel auersetur. Prius igitur exponit per contrarium, qualia Dominus auersetur. Apparet autem, subesse grauem occupatione. Dicturi enim forte erant Judæi: Si peccauimus, at placabimus Deum multis & optimis sacrificijs, obseruatione feriarum, ceremonijs, cantionibus, atq; id genus exercitijs. Respondet Dominus, se illa fastidire, nec posse ullo modo grata esse, tantum abest ut iram Dei placare & pro peccatis satisfacere queant. Interea non obscure hic legis omniumq; externorum operum imbecillitas, præterea ceremoniarum abrogatio declaratur.

Cum manus vestræ.) Caussa, cur non possint placere: quia omni genere scelerum ipsi adhuc sunt contaminati. Oportet persona prius esse accepta per fidem, quàm acceptetur aliquod eius opus, quamlibet in speciem sanctum & eximium. Sanguines pluratiuè, pro omni genere flagitiorum, maximè pro oppressione innocentum & imbellium, more Hebræo. ut Psal.51. Libera me de sanguinibus.

page.notes: Page number read as "22"; the digits are small and a reading of "23" is possible. Underlined words "auersetur" and "Sanguines" are marked as underlined, not italic. Handwritten annotations in the right margin ("Loco cordis inter na") are not printed and are left out. The paragraph opening "Lauate igitur cor.)" is a printed heading-like marginal line in the scan and is read as the start of a paragraph; the line "Lauate igitur cor.)" is copied in full. The final word of the text, "ces-", is uncertain and is followed by the catchword "se,ubi". The gathering signature "b 3" is uncertain.
